subject: Thermometer check: monthly burn corridor, PO on-ramp & next steps
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Shah <priyanka@frostlinehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Thermometer check: monthly burn corridor, PO on-ramp & next steps

Hi Priyanka — thanks again for carving out time this morning. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can align the procurement path cleanly: 

Recap from today's demo
- Primary workload: document triage + summarization for clinician notes (1–2k tokens per doc, mixed sync/async usage).
- Expected cadence: 400–2,000 calls/day initially, ramp over 3 months.
- Success metric: end-user latency < 350ms (95th) and predictable month-over-month cost.

Thermometer (monthly spend corridor) — please pick the range that best matches your current planning:
A) $8k–$20k / month
B) $20k–$50k / month
C) $50k–$120k / month

Procurement facts we need
- Primary purchasing vehicle (PO / credit card / card + PO after trial?)
- Minimum PO threshold and internal approval lead time (e.g., PO minimum $25k, legal review 2–3 weeks)
- Any required billing terms (NET30/45/60) and whether electronic invoicing is required

Suggested next steps
1) Fill the attached "thermometer-worksheet.xlsx" with a best-guess monthly burn and preferred purchasing lane (5–10 min).
2) If procurement wants, schedule a short call with your procurement contact + our legal ops — we can do a 30-min sync later this week.
3) Vivek will follow up with a rough unit-economics snapshot keyed to the selected corridor.

Attachments: thermometer-worksheet.xlsx (xlsx)

If you can reply with the selected corridor and procurement contact, we’ll prepare a tailored pricing sensitivity and a PO-onramp plan.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
(415) 555-0129

From: Priyanka Shah <priyanka@frostlinehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom@frostlinehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thermometer check: monthly burn corridor, PO on-ramp & next steps

Stephanie — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from our side after internal sync: 

Selected corridor
- Likely in the B/C overlap: roughly $30k–$60k/month for first 3–6 months, with a view to scale if latency/accuracy hit targets.

Procurement lane
- Procurement wants a PO for anything that will be invoiced > $50k/year (so annualized). For our expected burn that puts you above the 'card-only' lane unless we accept a short pilot on card.
- Typical legal review: 7–14 business days for a standard SaaS SOW; security questionnaire will be required.

Contacts
- Procurement inbox: procurement@frostlinehealth.com
- I'm happy to put Tom (VP Engineering) and procurement on a 30-min call tomorrow afternoon if that helps.

We can populate your worksheet tonight and should have it back by end of day. Also — we have a SOC 2 checklist request; can you point us to the right contact to feed that to our security team?

Best,
Priyanka
Head of Product
Frostline Health
priyanka@frostlinehealth.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Pricing sensitivity & on-ramp options for Frostline (rough numbers)

Stephanie / Marissa — quick internal note to shape the procurement conversation. Attaching a one-page sensitivity but calling out the key levers below. Attachment: pricing-sensitivity-rough.xlsx

Assumptions (rough):
- Token mix: avg 1.4k tokens per call (prompt + response)
- Volume: 1.2M–3M tokens/month (maps to Priyanka's $30k–$60k corridor at our baseline rates)

Baseline unit econ (per 1M tokens)
- Sticker RPU (hosted): $1,400 / 1M tokens
- Committed discounted RPU (annual commit): $1,050 / 1M tokens (25% off sticker)
- Reserved-dedicated profile (higher commitments): $850 / 1M tokens

Proposed pilot on-ramp to accommodate procurement constraints
- Phase 1 (30–60 days): Card + trial credits to validate latency/quality (no PO required)
- Phase 2 (30–90 days): 3–6 month committed slab (monthly invoicing, PO accepted) — target ~ $30k/mo commit to justify a 15–20% discount
- Phase 3: Annual commit option for deeper discounts and SLA guarantees (legal + ticketing)

Action items for external ask
- We can offer a 30% one-time pilot credit if they sign the SOW and agree to a follow-up PO conversation within 60 days.
- Need to confirm security contact to share SOC2 artifacts (Marissa to lead).

Notes: keep the corridor language high level when talking to procurement — they care about invoice cadence, PO threshold, and acceptance of electronic invoices.

— Vivek
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Thermometer check: monthly burn corridor, PO on-ramp & next steps

Hi Priyanka / procurement team — appreciate the quick turnaround. Based on your input, here are consolidated next steps and a practical PO on-ramp we can offer to reduce friction: 

Consolidated plan
- Immediate: Frostline populates the attached thermometer worksheet (thanks Priyanka) — we’ll use that to size a pilot.
- Pilot (30–60 days): Card + pilot credits (30% one-time credit) to validate performance and integration. No PO required for pilot.
- Short-term committed slab (3–6 months): Monthly invoices accepted; PO acceptable if monthly invoiced amount is supported by your internal process (we understand you prefer PO when annualized spend > $50k).
- Long-term: Option for annual commit with tiered discounts and SLA (we’ll include this in the SOW).

Documents & links
- Draft initial SOW attached: SOW-draft-initial.pdf
- HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/FRST-2026-038
- DocuSign (initial SOW ready for signature after a short procurement review): https://www.docusign.com/initial-sow/FRST-2026-038

Security / compliance
- Marissa will coordinate SOC 2 artifact delivery to your security team — marissa_cole@redwood.com. Please advise the best contact and preferred intake format (SaaS vendor portal vs email).

Proposed calendar options
- Thu 20 Aug, 11:00–11:30 PT — Procurement + Legal intro call
- Thu 20 Aug, 14:00–14:30 PT — Tech sync with Tom to validate token mix / latency targets

If that works, I’ll get the invites out and we’ll draft an invoice template for your procurement team to review.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting this over the finish line.

Best,
